deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a bibliographic note or library request slip. The main ink entry reads: 'Ebhardt. Gesetze, Verordnungen und Ausschreiben des Kön[iglichen] Consistorium zu Hannover. Bd. 1. 2. Hannover 1845'. This is Chr. H. Ebhardt's compilation of the laws, ordinances and circulars of the Royal Consistory of Hannover, volumes 1-2, Hannover 1845. Such a work covers church and school administration in the Kingdom of Hannover.

At lower right is the signature 'B. Riemann.', followed by a bracketed word that cannot be read with confidence (possibly a name or address qualifier). Other annotations:
- Faint pencil at the top centre: possibly 'f. d. Gymn...' or a similar shelf or user note.
- Red pencil at the left: a word, perhaps 'Verordnungen' or 'Bemerkungen'.
- Faint pencil in the middle: something like '...welche – Kirchen – Schulsachen' with a second line, partly struck through by a long pencil stroke.
- A large pencil scrawl, perhaps a numeral or librarian's mark.
- Red pencil at the lower left: apparently a date, 'Nov 18.58' or similar.
- Small pencil '44' at the right edge: the folio number.

The previous page, folio 43v, is a similar slip requesting volumes of the Journal de l'École polytechnique, signed the same way. So these are Riemann's library borrowing slips, plausibly from Göttingen around 1858.

If the slip is his, the subject (consistorial regulations on church and school matters) suggests a personal or family administrative concern rather than research. Riemann's father had been a Lutheran pastor in the Hannoverian church and died in 1855. This interpretation is a conjecture.

There are no derivations to reconstruct.

'44' at the right edge is the archival folio number, not content.
